quizzes.title: Women's T20 World Cup 2026 - MCQ
quizzes.passage: The ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 was one of the major events in the international cricket calendar, bringing national women's teams together in the Twenty20 format. The tournament was held over several weeks and was staged across a number of venues. Understanding how the event was structured helps explain how the final was reached. Two groups formed the opening phase. Each group contained the same number of teams, and every side played the other teams in its group in a round-robin format. The results of this phase determined which teams moved into the knockout rounds, where each match carried greater significance. The final was the last match of the competition. Individual players were also recognised with awards for their performances across the event. The tournament was organised by one national board, which worked with local venues to stage the matches. Several sides travelled to different grounds during the event, and supporters followed the progress of each team through the group stage and the knockout rounds. Players from many countries took part, giving the competition an international character. Results in the group phase were therefore central to the outcome of the event.

questions.q: Which body hosted the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026?
options: Board of Control for Cricket in India
questions.explanation: The booklet says the tournament was hosted by the England and Wales Cricket Board across 7 venues.

questions.q: How many teams played in each group of the tournament?
questions.explanation: The 12 teams played in 2 groups of 6 in a round-robin format.

questions.q: Shree Charani, the leading wicket-taker of the tournament with 14 wickets, belonged to which country?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Shree Charani as an Indian player and the leading wicket-taker with 14 wickets.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Only the top two teams from each group reached the semi-finals.
Reason (R): The tournament is held once every two years.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the two-year cycle does not explain why only the top two from each group advanced.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Beth Mooney
II. Lord's Cricket Ground
III. Australia
IV. Shree Charani

A. Venue of the 2026 final
B. Player of the Final and Tournament
C. Team that won the 2026 final
D. Record for most wickets by an Indian in a single edition
questions.explanation: Mooney was Player of the Final and Tournament, Lord's hosted the final, Australia won it, and Charani set the Indian record.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tournament:
I. Beth Mooney was the first player to win two Player of Tournament awards in T20 World Cup history.
II. Australia won its record-extending seventh title.
III. Only the top three teams from each group reached the semi-finals.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III is wrong because the top two from each group advanced.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
The tournament was held from 12 June to 5 July 2026.
The tournament was hosted across seven venues.
Shree Charani took 20 wickets as the leading wicket-taker.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The first two statements match the booklet, while the 20-wicket claim is wrong because the leading total was 14.

quizzes.title: Women's T20 World Cup 2026 - Typed Answer
quizzes.passage: Women's cricket has a regular place on the international calendar, and one of its notable events is a short-format tournament for national teams. The competition uses the Twenty20 format and brings together teams from around the world. Teams were arranged into groups for the early stage of the event, and each side played the others in its group. The knockout phase followed, and its matches carried greater weight than the group matches. Organising an event of this size required a host, and one national cricket board took on that responsibility. Matches were played at several grounds across the host country, with fixtures planned around each stage. The event was organised over a period of several weeks, with matches spread across that time. The final was the last match of the competition. Individual players were recognised for their performances, with awards given to those who stood out during the event. Fans followed the progress of the teams through each round, and the results of the group stage shaped the path to the final. The tournament gave the women's game a visible stage in the international calendar.

questions.q: Which cricket board hosted the tournament? (give the abbreviation)
questions.explanation: The booklet names the England and Wales Cricket Board as host, abbreviated ECB.

questions.q: Across how many venues was the tournament hosted? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet states the tournament was hosted across 7 venues.

questions.q: Which country's team won the 2026 final at Lord's? (one word)
questions.explanation: Australia defeated England in the final to win its record-extending seventh title.

questions.q: Who was the leading wicket-taker of the tournament with 14 wickets? (full name)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Shree Charani as the leading wicket-taker with 14 wickets.

questions.q: Which edition of the biennial tournament was held in 2026? (give ordinal, e.g. 9th)
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the 2026 event as the 10th Edition of the biennial tournament.

questions.q: In which year did Beth Mooney earn an earlier Player of Tournament award? (year)
questions.explanation: Mooney became the first player to win two Player of Tournament awards, in 2023 and 2026.

questions.q: Which player was named Player of the Final and Player of the Tournament? (full name)
questions.explanation: The booklet names Beth Mooney of Australia as Player of Final and Tournament.

quizzes.title: Sports and Youth Milestones - MCQ
quizzes.passage: July 2026 brought several developments across Indian sport, covering youth competition, tennis and cricket. A national youth sports event, the Khelo India Youth Games, has its next edition scheduled for a later date, and a new host state has been chosen for it. The previous edition was held in the year before, and one state was recognised as overall champion at that event. Separately, a former doubles world number one was appointed as an ambassador of an Asian tennis body, with a role to promote grassroots tennis across the continent. The same player is the only Indian tennis player to win an Olympic medal, and he has received a major national sporting award. In cricket, a teenager made his senior international debut in the shortest format of the game. The news items in this section are drawn from the month's sporting updates. Youth events, grassroots programmes and senior debuts are all part of the wider picture described here. Each item is reported separately, and each covers a different level of the sporting pathway.

questions.q: Which state will host the 8th Khelo India Youth Games?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports announced that Telangana will host the 8th edition in November 2026.

questions.q: In which year did Leander Paes win the Olympic bronze medal in men's singles?
questions.explanation: The booklet states Paes won bronze in men's singles at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics.

questions.q: In which city did Vaibhav Sooryavanshi make his senior T20I debut?
questions.explanation: He made his debut against England at Old Trafford, Manchester.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is India's youngest international cricket debutant.
Reason (R): Sooryavanshi made his senior T20I debut against England at Old Trafford.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the venue of the debut does not explain his age record.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Leander Paes
II. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
III. Bihar
IV. Maharashtra

A. Player Ambassador of the Asian Tennis Federation
B. India's youngest international cricket debutant
C. Hosted the 7th Khelo India Youth Games
D. Overall champion at the 7th Khelo India Youth Games
questions.explanation: Paes is the Asian Tennis Federation ambassador, Sooryavanshi is the youngest debutant, Bihar hosted the 7th edition, and Maharashtra was champion.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The 8th Khelo India Youth Games are scheduled for November 2026.
II. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made his senior T20I debut against Pakistan.
III. Leander Paes was honoured with the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II is wrong because the debut was against England.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi broke the record of Shafali Verma as India's youngest overall international debutant.
The 7th Khelo India Youth Games were hosted by Maharashtra.
Leander Paes won an Olympic bronze medal in men's singles.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The first and third statements match the booklet, while Bihar, not Maharashtra, hosted the 7th edition.

quizzes.title: Sports and Youth Milestones - Typed Answer
quizzes.passage: India's sporting structure includes ministries, national federations and state associations, each with a role in supporting athletes. A youth competition for young athletes forms one part of this framework, and it moves between host states from one edition to the next. Its recent editions have been held in different states, and each edition is run by its host. Former players have also been appointed to represent sporting bodies, and one such appointment this month involves promoting grassroots tennis across a continent. In cricket, a player made a senior international debut at a young age, and this debut was reported in the month's news. The news also covered a major national honour for a former tennis player. Coverage of the debut referred to a record set by a cricketer in an earlier era. These reports together show how youth events and senior sport are connected in the wider sporting landscape.

questions.q: Which state hosted the 7th Khelo India Youth Games? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet states the 7th Khelo India Youth Games were hosted by Bihar in 2025.

questions.q: Which state was the overall champion at the 7th Khelo India Youth Games? (one word)
questions.explanation: Maharashtra emerged as overall champion, followed by Haryana and Rajasthan.

questions.q: Give the full name of the national sporting award received by Leander Paes. (name of award)
accept: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award
questions.explanation: The booklet says Paes was honoured with the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award, also called the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award.

questions.q: At what age in years was Vaibhav Sooryavanshi when he made his international cricket debut? (number)
questions.explanation: He debuted at 15 years and 99 days, becoming India's youngest international cricket debutant.

questions.q: Whose record did Vaibhav Sooryavanshi break as India's youngest overall international debutant? (full name)
questions.explanation: He broke the record of Shafali Verma, who debuted at 15 years and 239 days in 2019.

questions.q: Against which country did Vaibhav Sooryavanshi make his senior T20I debut? (one word)
questions.explanation: He made his senior T20I debut against England at Old Trafford, Manchester.

questions.q: Which ministry announced the 8th Khelo India Youth Games? (name of ministry)
questions.answer: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, led by Mansukh Mandaviya, announced Telangana as host.

quizzes.title: Policy, Heritage and Observances - MCQ
quizzes.passage: Government policy on passenger vehicles has focused on reducing fuel use and emissions over time. Draft proposals for a new phase of the rules would tighten the standards that manufacturers must meet, with the aim of reducing average carbon dioxide output across a fleet. The rules cover a wide range of fuel types, including petrol, diesel, gas-based fuels and electric power. They apply to vehicles below a certain weight limit, so heavier vehicles fall outside their scope. Turning from transport to heritage, ancient India produced physicians whose work is recorded in classical texts. One such figure is remembered as an early pioneer of surgery, and his contribution has been honoured abroad. His writings belong to a group of foundational texts in the Ayurvedic tradition. The month's calendar also includes several international observances, each with a theme set for the year. These days honour cooperatives, national statistics and population. The items in this section cover policy, history and global days, and each is described briefly below.

questions.q: What does CAFE stand for?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that CAFE stands for Corporate Average Fuel Efficiency.

questions.q: Which body introduced CAFE norms in 2017?
options: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
questions.explanation: The booklet says CAFE norms were introduced by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency in 2017.

questions.q: Up to what vehicle weight do the CAFE norms apply?
questions.explanation: The norms apply to passenger vehicles weighing up to 3,500 kg.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The draft CAFE-III norms propose stricter fuel-efficiency and CO2 standards from April 2027.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

A is false but R is true
